{"evidence":[{"sentence_id":0,"text":"The Battle of Stamford Bridge took place at the village of Stamford Bridge, East Riding of Yorkshire, in England on 25 September 1066, between an English army under King Harold Godwinson and an invading Norwegian force led by King Harald Hardrada and the English king's brother Tostig Godwinson.","title":"Battle of Stamford Bridge"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" After a bloody battle, both Hardrada and Tostig along with most of the Norwegians were killed.","title":"Battle of Stamford Bridge"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" Although Harold Godwinson repelled the Norwegian invaders, his army was defeated by the Normans at Hastings less than three weeks later.","title":"Battle of Stamford Bridge"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" The battle has traditionally been presented as symbolising the end of the Viking Age, although major Scandinavian campaigns in Britain and Ireland occurred in the following decades, such as those of King Sweyn Estrithson of Denmark in 1069–1070 and King Magnus Barefoot of Norway in 1098 and 1102–1103.","title":"Battle of Stamford Bridge"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"Edith the Fair (Old English: \"Ealdgȳð Swann hnesce\" , \"Edyth the Gentle Swan\"; c. 1025 – c. 1086), also known as Edith Swanneck, was the first wife of King Harold Godwinson.","title":"Edith the Fair"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" \"Swanneck\" (or Swan-Neck) comes from the folk etymology which made her in Old English as \"swann hnecca\", \"swan neck\", which was actually most likely a corrupted form of \"swann hnesce, \"\"Gentle Swan\"\" \".","title":"Edith the Fair"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" She is sometimes confused with Ealdgyth, daughter of Earl Ælfgar of Mercia, who was queen during Harold's reign.","title":"Edith the Fair"}],"peer_messages":[],"previous_answer":"noanswer","question":"In which county is the English king Harold Godwinson buried?"}
